name: Serbia
headline: Serbia: +2.0% growth in 2025, 3.9% inflation, debt 42% of GDP
sections: Serbia is a $100.0 billion economy (2025), the world's 79th-largest of 215 measured. Real output grew +2.0% in 2025, slower than the world median of +3.5%. Income per person is $34K at purchasing-power parity (2025), against a world median of $21K. Manufacturing accounts for 12.7% of GDP (2024).

Consumer prices rose 3.9% in 2025, broadly within typical target ranges, down from 12.0% in 2022. Unemployment stood at 8.7% (2025), above the world median of 5.1%. Youth unemployment was 20.9% (2025).
Gross government debt is 42% of GDP (2025), a moderate level that has fallen from 54% in 2020. The general government balance is −2.2% of GDP (2025).
The current account balance is −4.9% of GDP (2025), a sizeable external financing need. Trade equals 113% of GDP (2025), a highly open economy. Net FDI inflows were 3.9% of GDP (2025).
IMF projections put government debt at 41% of GDP by 2031, broadly stable from today's level. Life expectancy is 76.0 years (2024). Population: 6.5 million (2025).
